knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Dtype and backend dispatch mismatch for scalar-tensor binary operations
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Backend dispatchers and kernels may not provide complete dtype coverage for scalar-tensor operations, causing combinations that succeed on one backend to fail on another.

risk_dimensions.shape: No specific shape boundary identified; varying tensor shapes including zero-dim and multidimensional may expose shape-dependent dispatch behavior.
risk_dimensions.dtype: Boolean tensor dtype with Python scalar operands, especially boolean scalars, and contrast with integer and floating scalar types.
risk_dimensions.device: CPU and CUDA backend dispatch differences for the same dtype and scalar combination.
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Binary operation dispatch state, including operator versus functional API and tensor-scalar operand order.

failure_mechanism.description: The CUDA backend dispatch path lacks a valid bool multiplication kernel for Python bool scalar operands, causing a runtime error even when the CPU path succeeds.

input_exploration: Enumerate scalar types such as bool, int, and float with tensor dtypes including bool, integer, and floating point
Run identical scalar-tensor operations on CPU and CUDA with both operand orders
Vary tensor shapes including zero-dim, scalar-like, 1D, and multidimensional
Test both operator syntax and functional API for the same dtype and scalar combination
Extend exploration to similar element-wise binary operations with scalar operands
constraint_awareness: CPU success does not guarantee CUDA kernel coverage for the same dtype and scalar combination
Python scalar type may dispatch differently than a tensor scalar due to type promotion rules
Backend kernels may not cover boolean or other low-precision dtype combinations
oracle_strategy: Compare CPU and CUDA behavior for the same dtype and scalar combination
Flag runtime errors indicating missing backend kernel implementations
Treat any CPU-supported dtype combination that fails on another backend as a potential dispatch bug

transferability.reason: The underlying principle applies to any element-wise binary operation that relies on backend dtype dispatch with scalar-tensor operands. Many operators have similar dtype coverage gaps across backends, making this a general testing principle beyond torch.mul.

llm_reasoning_guidance.important_considerations: Prioritize dtype and scalar-type combinations across device and operator variants. Backend kernel dispatch may be incomplete for certain combinations even when the API should support them.
generation_strategy: Generate harnesses that systematically enumerate scalar types, tensor dtypes, devices, and operator forms for element-wise binary ops. Do not hardcode the original torch.mul boolean scalar case.
